Rules / Modernization

SK1004 Use an extension block

A static class whose every member is an extension method on one receiver is the pre-C# 14 spelling of a single extension block, and the block is where properties, operators and static members on that receiver can also go.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floorC# 14.0
Since2.0

Why

The static-class-of-this-parameters idiom exists because C# had no way to say "these members belong to string". C# 14 has one. The block says the receiver once instead of once per member, and it is the only form that can carry an extension property, an extension operator or a static extension member — so a class in the old shape is not merely more verbose, it is a shape that cannot express the members somebody will want to add to it next. ⚠ The receiver stops being a parameter and becomes the block's subject, which is the whole readability argument: public static bool IsBlank(this string value) is a static method that happens to be callable with dot syntax, and extension(string value) { public bool IsBlank => … } is a member of string as far as every reader and every call site is concerned. Both call forms keep working — measured, not assumed: "x".Repeat(2) and StringExt.Repeat("x", 2) both compile against a block on SDK 10.0.400, so the rewrite is source-compatible in both directions.

Example

Instead of:

public static class StringExtensions {
    public static bool IsBlank(this string value) => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value);

    public static string Repeat(this string value, int times) => string.Concat(Enumerable.Repeat(value, times));
}

Write:

public static class StringExtensions {
    extension(string value) {
        public bool IsBlank() => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value);

        public string Repeat(int times) => string.Concat(Enumerable.Repeat(value, times));
    }
}

The ReSharper mapping

⚠ The export sets `resharper_convert_to_extension_block_highlighting` to `hint` and this rule defaults to `suggestion`, so reading the key lowers the severity. The gap is deliberate and it is about how new the syntax is rather than about how much the concept is worth: ReSharper shipped the inspection at hint in 2025.2 because extension blocks were days old and it did not want to light up every extension class in every solution at once. Skala's audience is a model writing the older dialect on purpose, which is exactly the population the concept is for, so it is reported at suggestion. ⚠ The inspection id is also not in `types-2026.xml`. ConvertToExtensionBlock appears in the editor_config_template export and not in jb inspectcode --dumpIssuesTypes, which is what RuleCatalogTests.EveryDeclaredReSharperKey_ExistsInTheExport reads — the two exports disagree because the issue-types dump predates the feature. The mapping is real and settable; it is the dump that is behind.

When it does not fire

⚠ One block or nothing, which is the restriction that makes the fix a rewrite rather than a guess. The rule fires only when every member of the class is an extension method, all of them on the same receiver type written the same way and bound to the same type, and all of them naming that receiver with the same identifier. A class mixing two receiver types needs two blocks and a decision about what order to put them in; a class mixing extension methods with plain statics needs the block to wrap a subset, and the subset need not be contiguous. Both are real conversions and neither is one this rule can perform without moving code a person wrote, so both are declined rather than half-reported. ⚠ A differing receiver *name* is declined for the same reason and it is not cosmetic. Merging this string value and this string s into one block means renaming an identifier inside a body, and a rename is a rewrite this rule has no way to bound — the name may be shadowed, captured or spelled in a nameof. The edits this fix emits are subtractive plus two braces, and that property is what makes it reviewable. ⚠ A method with its own type parameters is declined, because a receiver mentioning a method type parameter has to move to extension<T>(…) and the arity has to be reconciled across every member of the block; a class of this IEnumerable<T> helpers is the common case and it is exactly the one this rule does not attempt. ⚠ A `ref`, `in`, `ref readonly` or `scoped` receiver is declined, as is a receiver carrying an attribute: each of those is state on the parameter that the block's receiver declaration would have to reproduce, and the conversion stops being subtractive. ⚠ A `<param>` documenting the receiver withdraws the finding. The parameter ceases to exist, so the element would document nothing and the build gains a CS1572 on a public API — a fix that trades a suggestion for a warning. ⚠ A preprocessor directive anywhere in the class withdraws it, because the block's two braces are inserted at fixed points and a directive can put one of them inside a branch the other is not in. A comment inside any span the fix deletes withdraws it too; the deleted spans are only static and the receiver parameter, so this is rare and cheap to check. partial is excluded because the other part is not in front of the analyzer. Silent below C# 14, where the syntax does not parse — measured on the pinned Roslyn, where the same text at C# 13 recovers as a constructor named extension rather than reporting the feature. Marked unsafe: the conversion is source-compatible but it is not binary-compatible, since block members are emitted through a different metadata shape, so a published assembly needs the change reviewed rather than applied.
